learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and use of the principles of strength of materials.
Demonstrate the capacity for analysis and synthesis.
Acquire the capacity for effective problem-solving.
Develop the capacity to transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Capacity to apply knowledge to practice.
Acquire the capacity for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and continuous training.
Provide students with the basic theoretical knowledge necessary to understand the effect of different types of mechanical stresses on solids and components.
Introduce students to a calculation methodology under simplifying hypotheses that allows analyzing the response of resistant elements under the action of mechanical stresses.
The acquired competencies will serve as a basis for the design and calculation of more complex structures.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Elasticity and Strength of Materials
Object of Elasticity and Strength of Materials
Calculation of reactions and internal forces
Mechanical properties of a section. Area, center of gravity and moments of inertia.
Internal forces in a section: axial, shear, bending moment and torsional moment.
Relationship between Shear force (V) and Bending moment (M)
Stresses in circular and tubular shafts
Stress distribution in other types of sections
Stresses in pure bending. Navier's law
Calculation of keys and splined shafts
Calculation of bolted and riveted joints
Tangential stresses due to shear force
Graphical representation of the stress state. Mohr's Circle
teaching_methods: Completion of assignments, Reports, Papers and Evaluation Tests
Practical classes in classroom and laboratory
assessment_rules: For ordinary evaluation, each component (Continuous assessment tests, Theoretical-practical continuous assessment I, Theoretical-practical continuous assessment II) requires a minimum grade of 4/10. For the second call, students must re-take only the tests not passed in the first call, maintaining the minimum grade for each. For exceptional evaluation, there are three theoretical-practical knowledge tests, each weighted 40%, 40%, and 20%, respectively, all requiring a minimum grade of 4/10. In all cases, if any minimum grade is not achieved, the overall course grade will be calculated according to the UBU Evaluation Regulations. The evaluation system for exchange students may be modified if academic calendars of home and host universities do not coincide.
